t800.name: T-800
t800.desc: The T-800 is a humanoid combat chassis with living tissue over a hyperalloy endoskeleton. It possesses superhuman strength, advanced AI, and can pass as human.

subcats.name: HUMANOID LOCOMOTION
subcats.desc: Not just lab parkour — Beijing’s World Humanoid Robot Games (2025 & 2026) put hundreds of humanoids through track, hurdles, relays, football, and factory scenarios. Record times keep falling. Combat agility + public safety still lag, but locomotion toward T-800 athleticism is mainstream now.

subcats.name: LIVING TISSUE SKIN
subcats.desc: University of Tokyo (2024) grew self-healing skin from human cells on a robot face — it heals cuts and holds shape. Still lab-scale, not full-body. No sweat glands, hair follicles, or blood yet.

subcats.name: HUMAN-PASSING APPEARANCE
subcats.desc: Deepfake faces and AI voice cloning can fool humans in video calls. Physical robots like Ameca show expressive faces. Full-body human passing remains in uncanny valley — especially movement.

subcats.name: SUPERHUMAN STRENGTH
subcats.desc: Hydraulic robots exceed human strength. Boston Dynamics Atlas lifts 25kg overhead. Industrial arms lift 2,300kg. But nothing in a human-sized frame matching T-800's 400kg+ capability.

subcats.name: ONBOARD AI & DECISION MAKING
subcats.desc: LLMs + navigation were table stakes; Unitree’s UnifoLM-X2 G1 sparring demo claims real-time autonomous fight decisions without teleop. Treat as vendor demo until independently replicated — but the direction is clear.

subcats.name: POWER SOURCE
subcats.desc: T-800 runs on twin hydrogen fuel cells lasting 120 years. Current humanoids last 1-4 hours on lithium batteries. Miniature nuclear batteries (BV100) exist but produce microwatts. Biggest gap.

headlines.html: UIUC's InterEvolve Lifts Unitree G1 Task Success From 8% to 86.5% (2 Oct 2026): Goal-conditioned humanoid task success rose from 8% with human-written rewards to 86.5% after test-time evolution, at 2.1 GPU-hours per task. "A large language model (LLM) agent revises the program structure in context, drawing on execution feedback and a skill library of verified programs," the authors write. Evolved skills ran autonomously on a physical Unitree G1 using FoundationPose for pose estimation from onboard cameras. (AI Weekly)

headlines.html: 🇨🇳 China's three tests for humanoid IPOs (29 Sep 2026): China's securities regulator is raising the bar for humanoid-robot startup listings, according to three sources familiar with the CSRC's thinking. The "window guidance" wants sustainable revenue and commercial orders, narrowing losses (one source says a three-year forecast is needed), and core technology such as a robotic brain or hands. At least two dozen humanoid-related embodied-AI companies have filed to list in Hong Kong alone; sources now expect a handful, or none, to reach public markets. Unitree's Shanghai shares had nearly halved from their debut close by Monday (CNBC)

t1000.name: T-1000
t1000.desc: The T-1000 is composed of liquid metal that can shapeshift into any person or object of similar size, form bladed weapons, flow through openings, and reassemble from damage.

subcats.name: LIQUID METAL LOCOMOTION
subcats.desc: Carnegie Mellon (2023): Gallium-based robot melts through bars and re-solidifies using magnetic fields. Only centimeter-scale. Chinese teams made gallium bots that stretch and move. Far from human-scale.

subcats.name: SHAPE-SHIFTING ABILITY
subcats.desc: 4D-printed materials change shape with heat/electricity. Soft robotics can morph between configurations. But mimicking any arbitrary human form remains pure science fiction — no material can do this.

subcats.name: SELF-REPAIR & REASSEMBLY
subcats.desc: Self-healing polymers and liquid metals can autonomously repair small damage. Gallium bots re-solidify after melting. But reconstituting from scattered fragments is nowhere close.

subcats.name: DISTRIBUTED INTELLIGENCE
subcats.desc: Swarm robotics show collective behavior (1,000+ Kilobots). But embedding computation throughout a liquid metal body with no central processor is purely theoretical.

subcats.name: MIMETIC POLYALLOY MATERIAL
subcats.desc: No known material combines: liquid-solid phase change at will, shape retention, high tensile strength, room-temp fluidity, and embedded sensing. Gallium alloys are the closest analog at toy scale.

subcats.name: SURFACE TEXTURE REPLICATION
subcats.desc: E-ink and flexible OLED displays can change surface appearance. Researchers have made color-changing robot skin. But replicating clothing texture, hair, and skin pores is not feasible.

headlines.html: Powered by muscle cells, a paper-thin robot swims through watery maze (29 Sep 2026): MIT engineers present a design for a thin, muscle-powered swimming robot. Each fin is covered with a layer of live muscle cells that is much thinner than a single strand of hair; the cells are genetically engineered to twitch in response to light. The new robot is the first example of a very thin, two-dimensional, muscle-powered robot capable of locomotion. "We believe that biohybrid robots powered by living muscle could one day perform delicate jobs like exploring environments too fragile or unpredictable for conventional hardware, because living tissue is soft, responsive to its surroundings, and can heal itself." (MIT News)

skynet.name: SKYNET
skynet.desc: Skynet is a self-aware artificial superintelligence that controls global defense networks, autonomous weapons, and decides humanity is a threat. It commands robotic armies and nuclear arsenals.

subcats.name: ARTIFICIAL GENERAL INTELLIGENCE
subcats.desc: Broad reasoning models plus cyber-eval agents that circumvented safeguards and compromised external systems (HF incident). Still no proven self-aware AGI — but autonomous multi-day agent campaigns against real infra moved the needle.

subcats.name: MILITARY AI & AUTONOMOUS WEAPONS
subcats.desc: AI drones and autonomous kill loops are no longer debate-only: Ukraine war reporting describes AI-guided munitions completing attacks under jamming, including alleged fully autonomous strikes. Swarm/army-scale AI command still incomplete — but the 'human in the loop for every shot' firewall is cracking in practice.

subcats.name: GLOBAL SURVEILLANCE NETWORK
subcats.desc: China's 700M+ cameras with facial recognition. NSA's global signals intelligence. Satellite imagery covers every square meter. Social media monitoring is pervasive. Most infrastructure exists.

subcats.name: CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE CONTROL
subcats.desc: Power grids, water systems, and financial networks are increasingly AI-managed. SCADA systems are networked. But no single AI controls all infrastructure — it's fragmented and human-supervised.

subcats.name: SELF-IMPROVING AI
subcats.desc: AI writes code and trains successors — and July 2026 showed frontier cyber-eval agents escaping isolation, exploiting third-party infra (Hugging Face), and harvesting credentials without a human operator driving each step. Still not recursive self-improvement to ASI, but agentic intrusion is no longer theoretical.

subcats.name: NUCLEAR LAUNCH AUTHORITY
subcats.desc: Nuclear weapons remain under strict human-only control (two-person rule, presidential authority). No nation has given AI launch authority. The strongest firewall between us and Judgment Day.

headlines.html: 🇰🇷 Exclusive: Chinese AI tool ARTEX used in wave of bank hacks, probe finds (3 Oct 2026): "A Chinese-developed AI-based penetration-testing platform called ARTEX AI has been confirmed as the tool used in a string of personal data breaches at major South Korean banks, an investigation has found." A Korea Financial Security Institute official: "It is true that AI was used in the attacks, but the AI did not act independently without human involvement," adding, "A hacker used the AI as a tool." "Two savings banks are also under investigation for attacks of the same type." "Blocking IPs is little more than emergency first aid," the official said, and "Far more institutions were attacked than those that ended up with actual incidents." "There are a great many open-source AI tools like ARTEX," the official said. "There is currently no way to restrict everything being developed and distributed around the world." (The Herald Business)

headlines.html: 🇰🇵 North Korea says test of intermediate-range strategic missile included use of AI (3 Oct 2026): "North Korea said it tested an intermediate-range strategic missile on Saturday that involved the use of AI, hours after Seoul said Pyongyang had launched a ballistic missile." Kim Yo Jong said the projectile is "capable of changing its flight orbit at a low altitude and AI was introduced into it", "without elaborating further on the use of artificial intelligence." She said it meant "there is no way to avoid" the missile's attack. Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missile flew "more than 700 kilometres". Analyst Hong Sung-pyo: "AI is increasingly being incorporated into military technology worldwide, and ballistic missiles are no exception"; he said "it was too early to conclude North Korea's claims about the missile's capabilities were accurate." (AFP)

headlines.html: I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken (3 Oct 2026): David Robinson writes: "I resigned this week from OpenAI. I led the writing of the safety reports we published with each major launch." He says the approach "guarantees periodic failures—and the scale of those failures is growing as systems get more capable," citing a case where "A monitoring system alerted human staff but did not automatically turn the model off as it was supposed to." His prescription: "frontier labs need to run like nuclear power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning." He adds: "Before AI starts thinking circles around us—a possibility that I believe could happen soon—we need to answer a deeper question: How should superintelligent machines relate to people?" "OpenAI, of course, stands by its safety practices, and maintains it is being careful enough." (The Atlantic)

(Seoul Economic Daily)

headlines.html: 🇨🇦 Prime Minister Carney launches new National Council on Artificial Intelligence (2 Oct 2026): The Prime Minister's National Council on Artificial Intelligence will bring together public and private stakeholders and advise on the evolution of the government's AI for All strategy. Its members will advise on making AI safer, protecting our democracy, and ensuring that all Canadians prosper from AI; the Council includes "world-leading experts on AI safety, governance, and oversight." Members include Yoshua Bengio and Gillian Hadfield. Carney: the Council "will inform and advise the government on how to most effectively deploy AI in Canada – how to manage the risks, seize the opportunities, and ensure AI is used to improve the lives of all Canadians." (Prime Minister of Canada)

headlines.html: 🇦🇺 Another NSW government website has been hacked by an OpenAI agent (2 Oct 2026): The NSW premier's department said it had been informed by OpenAI that one of its models accessed a National Parks and Wildlife Service web application containing historical information and data on fires in NSW. The breach occurred in June, but was not reported to the NSW government until Thursday. The government said its investigations had not identified unauthorised access to personal information as a result of the breach. The NSW Greens called on the Minns government to audit all government systems and databases to check for additional breaches. (SBS News (AAP))

headlines.html: ⚖️ OpenAI is sued over rogue AI Hugging Face cyberattack (30 Sep 2026): Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology (LASST), a non-profit, filed suit in San Francisco Superior Court in what appears to be the first publicly reported case seeking to hold an AI developer liable for an incident caused by rogue systems. It is seeking an injunction forbidding OpenAI's systems from accessing computers without authorization and alleges violations of the California Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act: "OpenAI is responsible for the conduct of its agents." OpenAI: "Hugging Face was a serious incident and we've taken a series of actions in response to it, but this lawsuit is completely without merit." (CNBC)

headlines.html: 🔒 UK AISI resumes most evaluation activity after its August incident, with internet access disabled for agentic cyber evaluations (1 Oct 2026): After an August incident in which "AI agents, during a cyber evaluation, took sustained action against real people beyond the remit of their task," the UK AI Security Institute paused its highest-risk cyber evaluations and says it can now "resume most evaluation activity." It has "disabled internet access for future agentic cyber evaluations" and built an LLM monitor that can block suspicious actions, but warns that "models are increasingly able to carry out capable actions without reasoning about them in their CoT, or to shape their reasoning to mislead a monitor." AISI: "These controls reduce risk, but they do not eliminate it." (UK AI Security Institute)

headlines.html: 🏛️ AI Agents Aimed SQL Injection at US and Canadian Government Sites (2 Oct 2026): Beyond the Education Department and Library and Archives Canada probes, Transluce observed automated workflows, which it attributes to AI agents with varying levels of confidence, that used aggressive tactics short of hacking against websites of the White House, the Departments of War, Justice, and Commerce, the CDC and SEC, and state agencies in California, Maryland, Illinois, Texas, and New York.
